title: Tests for functional groups
keyIdea: Each test-tube reagent detects one functional group. Bromine water goes from orange to colourless with C=C. Sodium hydrogencarbonate fizzes with –COOH, and the CO₂ turns limewater cloudy. Warm acidified potassium dichromate(VI) goes from orange to green with primary and secondary alcohols and with aldehydes. Warm Tollens' reagent gives a silver mirror only with aldehydes. 2,4-DNP gives an orange precipitate with any C=O in an aldehyde or ketone. A negative result only rules out the group that test detects, so plan a sequence of tests and read the whole pattern.

kid: A functional group is the part of a molecule that reacts. Each group has its own test. Add a few drops of reagent to the liquid and watch. A change is a positive result.

Bromine water is orange. A C=C bond uses up the bromine, so it turns colourless. Sodium hydrogencarbonate fizzes with a carboxylic acid. The gas is CO₂, and it turns limewater cloudy. Alcohols do not fizz.

Warm acidified dichromate(VI) is orange. Primary and secondary alcohols turn it green. So do aldehydes. A tertiary alcohol leaves it orange. Warm Tollens' reagent gives a silver mirror, but only with an aldehyde. 2,4-DNP gives an orange solid with an aldehyde or a ketone.

No change is a result too, but it only tells you one group is missing. A ketone and a tertiary alcohol both leave dichromate orange. Use one more test to tell them apart. Write exactly what you see: colourless, not clear.
adult: This matches AQA A-level Chemistry 3.3.6.1, identification of functional groups by test-tube reactions. It is also Required Practical 6: tests for an alcohol, aldehyde, alkene and carboxylic acid. OCR A and Edexcel cover the same tests. OCR adds 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNP, Brady's reagent) for the carbonyl group. Students should state the reagent, the conditions and the observation, then link each positive result to a group.

Each test works through one reaction. Bromine adds across C=C (electrophilic addition), so its colour is lost. Carboxylic acids are acidic enough to release CO₂ from hydrogencarbonate; alcohols are not. Acidified dichromate(VI), Cr₂O₇²⁻, oxidises primary and secondary alcohols and aldehydes. It is reduced to green Cr³⁺. Tollens' reagent, [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺, oxidises only aldehydes and is reduced to silver. 2,4-DNP forms an orange 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone with any aldehyde or ketone.

Common mistakes: writing 'clear' for 'colourless', or 'turns red' for Tollens' (brick-red is Fehling's solution). Taking a green dichromate result as proof of an alcohol, when aldehydes also reduce it. The misconception that 'no change' means 'no functional group': a ketone or tertiary alcohol leaves dichromate orange. Expecting alcohols to fizz with NaHCO₃. Thinking one group masks another, when a molecule with two groups gives both positive tests.

In the lab, learners add four reagents to four liquids and read a result grid. They name four look-alike liquids using dichromate, Tollens' and 2,4-DNP. They pick precise observation wording, identify mystery liquids in as few tests as they can, and predict every positive test for molecules with two functional groups.

familyTip: Ask: "Which single test tells propanal from propanone, and what would you see?" (Tollens': a silver mirror with propanal only.) Then ask which test would not help (2,4-DNP: both give an orange precipitate).

lab.caption: Flagship lab: test four liquids, name look-alikes, word observations, solve mysteries and test two-group molecules.

practice.prompt: Which test distinguishes propanal from propanone?
practice.hint: Which reagent reacts with aldehydes but not ketones?
practice.explain: Propanal gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent; propanone does not. 2,4-DNP gives an orange precipitate with both, and neither has a C=C.

practice.prompt: Buta-1,3-diene has two C=C bonds. {a} mol of it reacts completely with bromine water. How many moles of Br₂ are used up?
practice.hint: Each C=C bond adds one Br₂ molecule across it, so count the C=C bonds in one molecule first.
practice.explain: Two C=C bonds per molecule means 2 mol Br₂ per mol of diene, so {a} mol uses {=2*a} mol Br₂.

practice.prompt: An unknown liquid leaves warm acidified dichromate(VI) orange. Which could it be?
practice.explain: 2-Methylpropan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol, so it is not oxidised and the dichromate stays orange. Butan-2-ol and ethanal both turn it green.

practice.prompt: {a} mol of 2-hydroxypropanoic acid, CH₃CH(OH)COOH, reacts with excess NaHCO₃(aq). How many moles of CO₂ are given off?
practice.hint: Which group reacts with a hydrogencarbonate: –OH or –COOH?
practice.explain: Only the –COOH reacts (1 mol CO₂ per –COOH); the alcohol –OH does not. So {a} mol of acid gives {a} mol CO₂.

pool.prompt: What is seen when bromine water is shaken with cyclohexene?
pool.hint: Clear and colourless do not mean the same thing.
pool.explain: The orange bromine is used up as it adds across C=C, so the mixture becomes colourless. Bromine water is already clear, so 'clear' earns no mark.

pool.prompt: Which compound fizzes with sodium hydrogencarbonate solution?
pool.hint: Only one of these is acidic enough.
pool.explain: Carboxylic acids release CO₂ from hydrogencarbonates. Alcohols and aldehydes are not acidic enough to react.

pool.prompt: A liquid turns warm acidified dichromate(VI) green. What can you conclude?
choices: It is a 1° or 2° alcohol or an aldehyde
pool.hint: Dichromate oxidises more than one kind of group.
pool.explain: Aldehydes are also oxidised by dichromate, so green shows a primary or secondary alcohol or an aldehyde. A further test such as Tollens' is needed.

pool.prompt: What is the positive result for an aldehyde with warm Tollens' reagent?
pool.explain: Ag⁺ is reduced to silver metal, which coats the tube as a mirror. Brick-red is Fehling's solution; orange to green is dichromate.

pool.prompt: In the Tollens' test, each mole of aldehyde (RCHO) reduces 2 mol of Ag⁺ to silver. How many moles of silver form from {a} mol of propanal?
pool.hint: Use the 1 : 2 ratio of aldehyde to silver.
pool.explain: 1 mol RCHO gives 2 mol Ag, so {a} mol propanal gives {=2*a} mol silver.

pool.prompt: Prop-2-en-1-ol, CH₂=CHCH₂OH, is tested. Which results are positive?
pool.hint: List the groups: C=C and a primary –OH.
pool.explain: The C=C decolourises bromine water and the primary alcohol turns dichromate green. Each group gives its own result; one does not hide the other.

pool.prompt: Ethanedioic acid has two –COOH groups. {a} mol of it reacts with excess NaHCO₃(aq). How many moles of CO₂ form?
pool.explain: Two –COOH groups give 2 mol CO₂ per mol of acid, so {a} mol gives {=2*a} mol CO₂.

pool.prompt: A liquid gives an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNP but no silver mirror with Tollens' reagent. What is it?
pool.hint: 2,4-DNP finds C=O. Tollens' finds only aldehydes.
pool.explain: The precipitate shows a C=O group; no mirror rules out an aldehyde, so it is a ketone. A tertiary alcohol has no C=O.

pool.prompt: Bromine water stays orange with a liquid. What does that tell you?
pool.hint: Each test rules out only its own group.
pool.explain: A negative bromine water test only rules out C=C. The liquid could still be an alcohol, acid, aldehyde or ketone.
